# temps_notification_provider_cloudflare (Resource)

A Cloudflare Email Sending notification provider: Temps sends alerts through Cloudflare's transactional email API. Temps never returns the provider's credentials, so changes made to them outside Terraform are not detected. Reading a provider of another kind is an error.

Import with `<id>`.

Required API key permissions: `notification_providers:read`, `notification_providers:create`, `notification_providers:write`, `notification_providers:delete`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_notification_provider_cloudflare" "mail" {
  name         = "Cloudflare mail"
  account_id   = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
  api_token    = var.cloudflare_email_token
  from_address = "alerts@mail.example.com"
  to_addresses = ["ops@example.com"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `account_id` (String) Cloudflare account ID that owns the Email Sending configuration.
- `api_token` (String, Sensitive) Cloudflare API token with the Email Sending permission. Temps never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `from_address` (String) Verified sender address, on a domain enabled for Email Sending.
- `name` (String) Display name.
- `to_addresses` (List of String) Recipients.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Send notifications through the provider.
- `from_name` (String) Sender name.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Import ID, `<id>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <id>. Temps never returns the API token, so set it in configuration again after importing.
terraform import temps_notification_provider_cloudflare.mail 8
```
